items.title: Mike Vax interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 29, 2022
items.q: I can tell you some of the guys that were there: Leon Breeden, Gene Hall, Jack Wheaton, Herb Wong, Matt Benton. They were in Stan’s suite and they were bemoaning about there’s no jazz at these conventions.

ctx.x: Yes. When you said that about putting personal expression into classical music it made me think of him because he did that. He could do that. Well this has just been a fascinating conversation, and I wonder, to wrap up, if you think back to when Stan and a few of the others sort of launched jazz education, could you envision what now in 2022, what the business of jazz education has arrived at? The state of it now?

You know it’s interesting, the original National Association of Jazz Educators, the original one, was basically Stan’s idea. And they were at I forget if it was Midwest or they were at one of the big conventions and the Kenton band had played. And I can tell you some of the guys that were there: Leon Breeden, Gene Hall, Jack Wheaton, Herb Wong, Matt Benton. They were in Stan’s suite and they were bemoaning about there’s no jazz at these conventions. There’s nothing going on what are we doing, and basically get…

love of the music. It’s how many trophies do we have in the band room. And so they’ll rehearse three, four, five tunes over and over and over all semester so they can go and win trophies. And that’s not education. It’s not what Stan envisioned, it’s not what most of us in jazz education envision. And one of the things that when I do, sometimes I’ll do a clinic at a state convention for the educators. And I’ll say, “How many of you actually delve into the history of jazz music with your students? How many of you…
